correctness.rationale: For a connected triangle-free simple G with n>=8 and codegree ≤2, every K=Δ_3(G)^vee face requires all triples connected. Thus all vertex pairs, path triples and exactly square tetrahedra occur; no size-five face exists since requiring >=2 edges per triple demands >=7 edges on five vertices contrary to Mantel. A path triangle with a unique common-neighbor pair collapses along its free nonedge. Every opposite square pair has exactly its two square common neighbors (codegree≤2), so collapse each square tetrahedron along one path triangle, then its other triangle along the now-free diagonal. These removals do not interfere between squares because a shared opposite pair would violate codegree. The survivor is a triangulation of S(G) plus precisely L distance-≥3 edges, so the Alexander dual is S(G)∨(∨^L S¹). Integral combinatorial Alexander duality and UCT imply H_(n−5)(Δ_3)=Z^b2 ⊕Tor H1(S(G)), H_(n−4)=Z^(b1+L), others zero, with no unsupported natural splitting assertion. Shellability obstruction follows nonzero next-to-top homology for a pure cut complex. Independently constructed the two-cubes-glued-along-a-face example from edges and verified n=12, e=20, squares=11, max codegree=2, L=20, with square complex homotopy ∨²S²; hence H7=Z²,H8=Z²⁰. Inspected full verifier including direct free-coface tests and Smith calculations for grid, torus, Klein bottle, and cubes. General argument is mathematical, not inferred from seven test graphs.

value.rationale: It translates overlapping four-cycle geometry to the complete integral homology of ordinary three-cut complexes, including next-to-top free classes and torsion from nontrivial square fillings. This substantially extends the edge-disjoint-square top-degree-only result and gives useful non-shellability tests and natural cube/periodic-grid examples.

limitations: Requires connected triangle-free simple graphs n>=8, codegree≤2; no assertion for higher codegrees or triangles or ordinary cut-complex homotopy. Literature residual: Equivalent square-completion formula may exist in unindexed Stanley–Reisner or clique-hypergraph terminology. Only homology of Δ_3, not its full homotopy, is established; the dual K is the one with explicit wedge decomposition. The CW square filling need not be aspherical or torsion-free; UCT transfer is essential.
